group.passage: Some first-aid ideas have been passed from parent to child for years, but doctors say they are wrong and can even make things worse. Here are six common myths about first aid, each followed by what you should do instead.

passage_parts.label: A
passage_parts.title: Seizures
passage_parts.text: You may hear, “Push something into the person’s mouth so they won’t swallow their tongue.” In fact, nobody can swallow their tongue, and objects in the mouth can hurt the teeth or jaw. Move hard things away, turn the person onto one side, and call for help if the seizure lasts over five minutes.

passage_parts.label: B
passage_parts.title: A Bleeding Nose
passage_parts.text: Many people say, “Lean your head back.” In fact, this lets blood run down your throat. Sit up, lean forward, and hold the soft part of your nose closed for ten minutes. If it is still bleeding after twenty minutes, see a doctor.

passage_parts.label: C
passage_parts.title: Burns
passage_parts.text: Some people say, “Put butter or toothpaste on it.” In fact, home remedies like these do not help. Hold the burn under cool running water for 15 to 30 minutes. Never put ice on it, and do not break any blisters.

passage_parts.label: D
passage_parts.title: Swallowed Poison
passage_parts.text: Some people say, “Make the person throw up.” In fact, you should not do this unless a doctor or a poison center tells you to. Call for help right away, and never give food or drink to someone who is not awake.

passage_parts.label: E
passage_parts.title: Bleeding Cuts
passage_parts.text: Many people say, “Take off a bloody cloth to check the cut.” In fact, if blood soaks through, you should leave the cloth where it is. Put a new one on top and keep pressing. Lifting the cloth to look can make the bleeding harder to stop.

passage_parts.label: F
passage_parts.title: Snake Bites
passage_parts.text: In movies, people often suck the poison out. In real life, this does not work, and neither does cutting the wound. Stay calm and keep still. Take off rings and watches before the area starts to swell, and get to a hospital quickly. Do not try to catch the snake.

At a summer camp, the nurse gets three calls in one afternoon: a boy has a bleeding nose, a girl has burned her hand on a hot pot, and a camper has been bitten by a snake. Which entries should the nurse read to help these campers?

In F (Snake Bites), which verb means “to become bigger than usual, often after an injury”?（簡答題，2分）

1.strategy_zh: 用 burn、butter、toothpaste 回到 C；suggest 後面的動詞用 V-ing，put 變 putting 要多寫一個 t。

回到 C：關於燙傷，有人說要對奶油或牙膏做什麼？
原文 “___ butter or toothpaste on it.”；把這個動詞改成 V-ing，注意拼字。

2.explanation_zh: E（Bleeding Cuts）說 if blood soaks through, you should leave the cloth where it is（如果血滲透了布，布要留在原處），再蓋一塊新的上去繼續壓。空格放在 A cloth 後面修飾它，表示「被血浸濕的布」，要用過去分詞 soaked（soaked with blood＝被血浸透的）。
evidence: In fact, if blood soaks through, you should leave the cloth where it is.
2.strategy_zh: 用 cloth、blood、cut 回到 E；空格修飾前面的名詞 cloth，布是「被」浸濕的，用過去分詞。
hints: 空格修飾前面的 A cloth，而且布是「被」血弄濕的：要填過去分詞。
回到 E：血怎麼樣了的時候，布還是要留在傷口上？
原文 if blood ___ through；把這個動詞改成過去分詞。

3.explanation_zh: 三通電話分別是流鼻血、手被熱鍋燙傷、被蛇咬，對應 B（A Bleeding Nose）、C（Burns）、F（Snake Bites）。E 講的是割傷流血，雖然也是「流血」，但不是鼻子；D 講的是吞下毒物，雖然也有「毒」，但被蛇咬不是把毒吞下去；A 癲癇發作和三件事都無關。
evidence: Sit up, lean forward, and hold the soft part of your nose closed for ten minutes.
Hold the burn under cool running water for 15 to 30 minutes.
Take off rings and watches before the area starts to swell, and get to a hospital quickly.

option_notes_zh.A: 三件事都和癲癇發作無關；這一則講的是發作時不要往嘴裡塞東西。
option_notes_zh.D: 這一則講的是「吞下毒物」時不要催吐；被蛇咬的毒是從傷口進入，不是吞下去，應該看 F。只對上「毒」這個字。
option_notes_zh.E: 這一則講的是割傷的布被血浸濕時不要拿掉；男孩是流鼻血，應該看 B。只對上「流血」這個字。

3.strategy_zh: 需求對應條目題：先把三個需求各自寫成關鍵詞（鼻子流血、燙傷、蛇咬），再逐則看標題與內容。只對上一個字（bleeding、poison）的條目要再確認情況是不是一樣。
hints: 三通電話各要找一則：流鼻血、燙傷、被蛇咬。
「流血」不只一則，「毒」也不只一則：哪一則講的是鼻子？哪一則講的是被蛇咬？
答案是講鼻子流血、燙傷、蛇咬的三則；割傷和吞下毒物是不同的情況。

B: Many people say, “Lean your head back.”
In fact, this lets blood run down your throat.
C: Hold the burn under cool running water for 15 to 30 minutes.
D: Some people say, “Make the person throw up.”
E: Many people say, “Take off a bloody cloth to check the cut.”
F: Take off rings and watches before the area starts to swell, and get to a hospital quickly.

4.explanation_zh: F 說被蛇咬後要在 the area starts to swell（被咬的部位開始腫起來）之前拿下戒指和手錶。swell 是動詞，意思是「（受傷後）腫脹、變得比平常大」，符合題目的英文定義。starts to 後面是原形動詞，照文中的字形寫 swell。
evidence: Take off rings and watches before the area starts to swell, and get to a hospital quickly.
4.strategy_zh: 依英文定義找字：題目限定 F、限定動詞；定義說「受傷後變得比平常大」，找為什麼要先拿下戒指和手錶的那一句。
hints: 要找一個動詞，意思是「受傷後變得比平常大」。
看 F：為什麼被蛇咬後要先拿下戒指和手錶？
答案在 before the area starts to ___；寫這個動詞。

translation_zh.text:
【引言】有些急救觀念一代傳一代流傳了好多年，但醫師說它們是錯的，甚至會讓情況更糟。以下是六個常見的急救迷思，每一個後面都附上你應該怎麼做。
【A 癲癇發作】你可能聽過：「把東西塞進他嘴裡，他才不會把舌頭吞下去。」事實上，沒有人會把舌頭吞下去，而嘴裡的東西反而會弄傷牙齒或下巴。把周圍的硬物移開，讓他側躺；如果發作超過五分鐘，就打電話求救。
【B 流鼻血】很多人說：「把頭往後仰。」事實上，這會讓血流進喉嚨。應該坐直、身體往前傾，捏住鼻子柔軟的部分十分鐘。如果二十分鐘後還在流血，就去看醫生。
【C 燙傷】有人說：「塗奶油或牙膏。」事實上，這類偏方沒有幫助。應該用流動的冷水沖燙傷處 15 到 30 分鐘。千萬不要放冰塊，也不要弄破水泡。
【D 吞下毒物】有人說：「讓他吐出來。」事實上，除非醫生或毒物諮詢中心要你這麼做，否則不要催吐。要馬上求救，而且絕對不要給失去意識的人吃東西或喝東西。
【E 割傷流血】很多人說：「把沾了血的布拿掉，看看傷口。」事實上，如果血滲透了布，布要留在原處，再把一塊新的布蓋在上面繼續壓住。掀開布來看，反而會讓血更難止住。
【F 被蛇咬】電影裡的人常常把毒吸出來。在現實中，這麼做沒有用，把傷口割開也沒有用。要保持冷靜、不要亂動。在被咬的部位開始腫起來之前拿下戒指和手錶，並且盡快去醫院。不要試著去抓蛇。
